answers.answer: At the start of an Exile’s turn, Wake first checks Usurper victory, then an Exile holding the Oathkeeper title flips it to Usurper. Thus after taking the title during Act, the first Wake only flips it; the first possible Usurper win is the following Wake, or the end of round 8 if still Usurper then. If someone takes the title meanwhile, the win is prevented; retaking it resets the title to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Oathkeeper title and four Oaths: “Victory was checked before this flip”; losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it.

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary win also requires the Exile to have the true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck by all players combined. For Conquest and Sanctuary, “most” means strictly more than every other player; ties do not count.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Oathkeeper title and four Oaths; “For Conquest/Sanctuary ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player.”

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. The Chancellor wins unless a qualifying Citizen Successor wins alone instead. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll, so an Exile Oathkeeper cannot permit it.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Stable regime: round-end timing, thresholds, winner, and Exile title exception.

answers.answer: Round 8 ends automatically. Check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins, with a qualified Citizen Successor winning alone instead of Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions prioritized Conquest → Rebellion → Sanctuary → Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, again with a qualified Citizen Successor replacing Chancellor. A Citizen does not win by a Vision or Usurper status.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → War exhaustion: exact four-step priority and simultaneous Vision priority.

answers.answer: A Citizen Successor wins when Chancellor would win if they meet the Oath’s goal: Supremacy—hold more relics and banners than Chancellor and every other Citizen; People—hold Darkest Secret; Protection—hold People’s Favor; Devotion—hold Grand Scepter. Holding the goal does not itself end the game. Citizens and Chancellor cannot win by a true Vision or as Usurper.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table; “Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper”; Successor resolves whenever Chancellor would win.

answers.answer: At Wake, if holding People’s Favor, choose either to put 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 favor from it to a least-full suit bank, choosing among tied banks. Never remove its last favor: if it has 1, add 1 if able; if you have none, do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, make the choice twice. Only after these choices, check whether it has 6 or more favor and flip it to Mob. Becoming Mob at this final check does not cause another payment that Wake.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Wake: mandatory order, item 1.

answers.answer: Rest in order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply; save unspent Supply; then optionally use Rest powers once each in chosen order. Chancellor refreshes by personal-bank warbands: 18+ gives 6, 11–17 gives 5, 4–10 gives 4, 0–3 gives 3. Exile: 9+ gives 6, 4–8 gives 5, 0–3 gives 4. Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost. Then move the Supply marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply).
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Rest: mandatory order, items 1–5.

answers.answer: Search chooses either the world deck or the discard pile for the pawn’s region, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, or 4 at 3–5; holding Darkest Secret makes that cost 2, with other applicable modifiers still applying. Draw 3, unless source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces it; cannot voluntarily stop early. From the world deck draw one at a time; upon a Vision, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision from a discard pile neither stops drawing nor advances the track.
answers.evidence: Actions → Search: costs and Vision distinction between world deck and discard.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region’s pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; choose order for multiple discards, and never use the same-region pile. For a card in hand or an adviser, use the pile after your pawn’s region. For a card at a site in another region, use the pile after that card’s region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching suit bank; secrets on it go to the acting player’s board facedown.
answers.evidence: Actions → Search, Discard destinations paragraph.

answers.answer: Adviser limit is up to 3 total, faceup and facedown combined. Before exceeding it, discard an adviser, respecting locks; if the incoming card changes the limit, check the new limit before playing it, using the lowest of multiple limits. Facedown advisers have no suit, restriction banner, or power; any card, including site-only cards and Visions, can be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser may be played faceup legally or discarded as a minor action; it may be peeked at. A faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will, only when a rule permits or requires it. A true Vision is revealed only by an Exile, in the separate Revealed Vision slot, not as an adviser; revealing replaces and discards the old revealed Vision. Chancellor/Citizens may hold a true Vision facedown but cannot reveal it.
answers.evidence: Actions → Search: Adviser and True Vision bullets; Adviser retention table.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply: at your pawn’s site, put 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice (no favor or secrets), then gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board (Citizens gain purple). No rule is needed, but it is not remote; relics and ruins are ineligible. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn’s site. Option A: put 1 secret on it and gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card’s suit bank. Option B: put 2 favor on it and gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser; if none match, gain zero secrets. Facedown advisers never match. Costs are still paid if gain is zero; finite favor/warband sources yield only available pieces, secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Actions → Muster and Trade.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A facedown relic must be at your site; pay its printed site cost, then hold it faceup in your personal bank. Relics held by players or in the Reliquary cannot be recovered. Either banner may be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. To recover People’s Favor, pay any amount of favor strictly greater than its current favor onto it; distribute its old favor singly to suit banks, starting at any chosen bank and proceeding away from the world deck through successive banks, wrapping as needed; do not return old favor to previous holder, and flip Mob to normal. To recover Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets onto it; new holder takes 1 old secret and previous holder takes the rest. Recovering it from yourself returns all old secrets to you; from shared bank the remainder stays there. Recovery has no banner seizure penalty.
answers.evidence: Actions → Recover: relic and banner costs/effects.

answers.answer: To recover another player’s Darkest Secret, that player must have at least one suited card at their pawn’s site whose suit matches none of their faceup advisers. One unmatched card is enough even if other site cards match. An empty site or ruin-only site protects it because there is no suited card there. If the holder has no faceup advisers but has a suited site card, that card matches none and the secret is recoverable. Facedown advisers and ruins have no suit. Recovery from yourself or the shared bank ignores this protection.
answers.evidence: Actions → Recover, Darkest Secret protection corrected by errata.

answers.answer: For 2 Supply, choose as defender any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there; if no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn’s site, and if the defender rules that site you must target it. You may also target any of defender’s sites anywhere on the map (1 defense die each). If defender’s pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to banner resources), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice); a co-located defender’s relic alone satisfies the local-target requirement. Form pools, apply modifiers and title defense bonus, then battle plans and combat. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; if Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
answers.evidence: Actions → Campaign, steps 1–3.

answers.answer: The attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in the attacking force. Defense dice include dice from targets and applicable modifiers (Oathkeeper +1, Usurper +2); roll defense first. Each shield counts, each double-symbol doubles shields (multipliers stack), then add all defending warbands at targeted sites and the defender’s board force if their pawn is at the attacker’s site or any targeted site; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Doubles multiply shields only. Roll attack: each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband; count full swords, and each pair of hollow swords adds 1 (leftover single adds zero). The attacker may sacrifice surviving own force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack strictly exceeds defense; ties or lower mean defender wins.
answers.evidence: Actions → Campaign, steps 2, 4–5.

answers.answer: After attacker victory, first defender kills half the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board; then resolve defeated battle-plan effects. After defender victory, attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, survivors stay on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor’s board, while surviving Citizen board warbands remain on those boards. If attacker won, it may place any number—including zero—of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites; zero leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. Take all targeted relics and banners. On any banner seizure other than Recover, burn 2 banner resources to minimum 1; People’s Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor was targeted, attacker may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply and may independently burn half defender’s board favor, rounded down; respect travel restrictions, and Shrouded Wood’s enemy ruler chooses the forced destination. Finish effects: on attacker victory resolve targets then attacker’s victorious effects; on defender victory skip attacker’s targets but resolve defender’s victorious effects. Finally discard plans saying “At end, discard.” Supremacy title transfers at Campaign end, not during temporary loss of site rule.
answers.evidence: Actions → Campaign, steps 6–8 and Imperial defense.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally; other non-attacking Citizens may join with defender’s permission if their pawn is at attacker’s site or a targeted site. Apply modifiers ruled by defender/Allies. Their powers are shared as one defending side for “you,” “your enemy,” and “defender,” while “your site/board” remains each player’s own. Allied board warbands add defense only if their pawn is at attacker’s site or a targeted site. Defender/Allies can use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not another player’s advisers; each shared plan is usable once total by one user, who pays. Declared defender chooses order, timing, and priority when Allies disagree. Chancellor chooses Imperial defending casualties; site survivors go to Chancellor’s board, Citizen-board survivors stay there. In a Citizen’s Campaign against Chancellor or another Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial; a Chancellor attack makes the Citizen defender non-Imperial. It does not make all Citizens non-Imperial.
answers.evidence: Actions → Campaign: defender selection and Imperial defense.

answers.answer: Base Travel costs by origin/destination region: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, any region 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Move to any different site; garrisons stay put. Reveal a facedown destination and place its printed favor/secrets from shared bank and relics facedown from relic deck. Apply fixed-number cost first, then increases/decreases; free Travel is final, setting Supply payment to zero despite increases. Site entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by a power. Travel powers can increase costs, while the final free-Travel rule applies to all Travel, including banishment.
answers.evidence: Actions → Travel: cost table, reveal effect, and cost order.

answers.answer: During play, the Grand Scepter holder (even an Exile) may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, or exile another Citizen; cannot make an offer on the turn they took the Scepter. A Citizenship offer promises exactly one Reliquary relic; the parties may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may peek at Reliquary relics. On acceptance, recipient flips to Citizen and replaces all own board/map warbands with purple; if short, recipient chooses which to remove/replace. They discard revealed Vision, flip Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end their Act if it is their turn, and refresh to full leftmost Supply. Exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers use those status-conversion steps without a negotiated offer, required Scepter gift, or invented exchange; only an actually removed Reliquary relic uncovers its modifier.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play → Grand Scepter, Offer, Acceptance, Forced Citizenship.

answers.answer: Chronicle Oath: if victory was by Vision alone, next Oath matches that Vision; otherwise, including multiple victory methods, winner chooses any Oath except the current one. Save it in World Box. For free Chronicle Citizenship, no Scepter permission, Reliquary relic, or resource payment is needed. If the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards (including boxed) to Exile, then they may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; each accepting Exile flips to Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site. Rebuild world deck from remaining in-play denizens: top stack 10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12; middle 15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions = 18; rest of denizens below. The Chronicle aid’s “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; top stack is not 14 cards.
answers.evidence: Writing the Chronicle, steps 1–2 and 9.
